title: Temporal Decomposition of Byte Stream Parsing
pattern: Splitting network reading and parsing into separate, sequentially invoked structures where both must understand the underlying wire format invariants.
why_bad: Information leakage. To read the correct body length, the reader must parse protocol headers (e.g., `Content-Length`), resulting in duplicated protocol knowledge across multiple modules.
detection: Distinct structures processing the same input stream in sequence, where both contain code dealing with underlying wire protocol details (e.g., matching HTTP headers in multiple files).
counterexample: A clean layer boundary where Layer 1 parses raw byte packets and passes complete frames, while Layer 2 processes high-level messages.
source: *A Philosophy of Software Design* by John K. Ousterhout (Chapter 5, "Information Hiding (and Leakage)", p. 32).
